pr_title: Bluetooth: TMAP: Add role validation for bt_tmap_register
pr_body:
Add validation that the device supports the role
set by bt_tmap_register.

fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/60495

issue_context.title: LE audio TMAP: Add role verification
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
want to discuss if we should add any abstraction layers for the different TMAP roles in tmap driver?

each TMAP role requires some special settings and low layer profile procedures.
![image](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/assets/3600912/82a9ce78-c758-4bc7-b6e7-0f2f6652777d)
but there is no more implementation for these in tmap.c
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/subsys/bluetooth/audio/tmap.c

we do these in demo apps:
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/60288/commits/b926b294610a255eb81079a68764e3a486848e95#diff-cc104b7b2a9cb82bee5f3b6d56b8f3a54b4d2660731f7546c26bbd2eca310f5f
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/56686/commits/f4f0f003a4e6cb3d88a7049a0c59625588eced32#diff-48dd3e98c744416052457825e6733baa10cfc8d0bfa0644aee65dddab49317c4

**Describe the solution you'd like**
add more apis to simplify the TMAP role usages.
comments: Indeed. `bt_tmap_register` and `bt_tmap_set_role` should return an error if the supplied role is not supported by the device

review_comments:
This is not specific for this PR, but also shows up other places where `CHECKIF` is used, and will be compiler dependent:
If the KCONFIG option `NO_RUNTIME_CHECKS` is set to 'y' a compiler may emit the following warning: `static bool valid_tmap_role defined but not used`

suggestions for fixing this?

Two ways we can apply is to guard this call with an IS_ENABLED, or instead of having `CHECKIF` in the call, we can change all the checks in the functions to use `CHECKIF` to that if `NO_RUNTIME_CHECKS` then the function is just a no-op.

But you have a good point that we should do that here

Looking at the macro it is defined as

```c
#elif defined(CONFIG_NO_RUNTIME_CHECKS)
#define CHECKIF(...) \
	if (0)
#else
```

With `if (0)` the code is still compiled, but not linked, and should thus not have any issues. Will leave as is
Yes, the code compiles and works fine as is, the only issue is that we get a compiler warning, that shouldn't be there.
